properties.decision:
RECORDED AS A MEASURED FIELD DEFECT PLUS AN OPEN QUESTION. Reported 2026-08-05 from the hxm_program session, item 4 of six.

WHAT WAS OBSERVED, in the reporter's words: "After the capture batch, `loop_status` reported `unsurfaced_gaps: 0` — but `detect_gaps` had never been run, and when it did run it found 3 REAL PHASE-LEVEL GAPS." Their conclusion is the sentence worth keeping: "AN AGENT THAT TRUSTS `clean: true` HAS NO REASON TO RUN THE DETECTOR."

⭐ WHY THIS IS NOT SIMPLY A MISSING TIMESTAMP. `loop_status` is the call the SessionStart hook and the server instructions both push every session to run FIRST, described as "the one cheap call that says what the coherence loop is owed". It is the orientation surface. A false clean there does not mislead one report — it tells the agent the loop is settled at the exact moment the loop has not started.

AND IT COLLIDES WITH AN ACCEPTED DECISION RATHER THAN JUST BEING AN OVERSIGHT. `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` is ACCEPTED: "Loop debt is computed from graph state, never from run history" — with the stated reason that LOOKING IS NOT WRITING, so counting runs would reward bookkeeping. That ruling is right and it is exactly what produces this: a gap that has never been detected is not IN the state, so state-derived debt cannot see it. The defect is downstream of a correct decision, which is why it needs a decision rather than a patch.

THIS IS THE THIRD INSTANCE OF ONE SHAPE IN A WEEK, AND THE PATTERN NOW HAS A NAME IN THIS PROJECT'S OWN RECORD: [BL-206], the coherence gate reporting OK over 20 artifacts it never swept; [BL-208], the export-lineage guard reporting nothing because a shallow checkout meant it could not see `HEAD~1`; and `dec:no-design-here-never-looked`, filed from the same report, where "this directory has no design yet" was asserted without looking. The carried sentence from BL-208 was "a guard whose no-op path is silent will eventually run nowhere and say so to nobody". THIS IS THE READING-SURFACE VERSION: A COUNT THAT CANNOT DISTINGUISH ZERO FROM UNMEASURED READS AS ZERO.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN. (a) THE REPORTER'S SUGGESTION — a `last_gap_scan` timestamp, or a `scanned: false` field. Cheap and directly answers it. Counter: a timestamp IS run history, which is what `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` deliberately excluded, so taking it means amending that decision rather than quietly contradicting it — and the amendment has to explain why THIS history is legitimate when run-counting was not. The distinguishing argument, if it is taken: recording that a detector RAN is not the same as crediting the agent for running it; one is a property of the reading, the other is a score. (b) MAKE THE ABSENCE STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN TEMPORAL — report `unsurfaced_gaps` as unknown until a scan has ever produced a gap-or-none result for the current graph revision, keyed on state rather than on time. Fits the accepted decision without amending it. Counter: needs a notion of "the graph revision a scan covered", which does not exist. (c) NEVER REPORT A ZERO — say "run detect_gaps" whenever the count is zero, whatever the cause. Crude, honest, costs nothing, and would have prevented the observed failure. Counter: it makes a genuinely clean design nag forever, which is how a signal gets trained to be ignored — the exact failure [BL-191] fixed for volatile artifacts. (d) LEAVE IT AND RELY ON THE STOP HOOK, which the reporter notes DID catch this ("the stop-hook nudge caught this — 'bookkeeping is not the loop' — which worked"). Counter: the hook fires at the END of a session, and the false clean is read at the START.

NOT CHECKED, and it widens or narrows this considerably: whether the other zero-valued counters in `loop_status` have the same property — `unexamined_claims`, `unproven_capabilities`, `undispositioned_drift`, `unwritten_answers`. If they are all state-derived in the same way, this is one defect with five faces rather than one field.
properties.name: OPEN — loop_status reports unsurfaced_gaps 0 before detect_gaps has ever run, so "clean" and "never scanned" are the same answer
properties.rationale:
Filed as its own node rather than a backlog row because the fix is not obvious and the obvious fix contradicts an accepted decision. `dec:loop-status-state-not-history` says debt is computed from state and never from run history, for a good stated reason; a `last_gap_scan` timestamp is run history. Whoever takes this has to either amend that decision with an argument for why recording a reading differs from scoring an agent, or find a state-shaped answer. A backlog row would have carried the symptom and lost the collision.

The three-instance pattern is written out because this is the point at which it stops being a coincidence: two gates and now the orientation call, all reporting a confident absence they never measured. Naming it once, with the instances, is cheaper than finding it a fourth time.

The unchecked item — whether the other four counters share the property — is stated because it decides whether this is one row or five, and nobody has looked.
